Indirect standardization from aggregate observed and expected events

Source: R/ds.vertStandardization.R
ds.vertIndirectStandardization.Rd

Computes a standardized mortality ratio (SMR) or standardized incidence ratio (SIR) from caller-supplied aggregate observed and expected events. The two labels share the same estimator; measure records the intended scientific interpretation. The confidence interval is the exact central Garwood interval for a Poisson count with fixed expected events.

Usage

ds.vertIndirectStandardization(
  observed,
  expected,
  measure = c("SMR", "SIR"),
  scale = 100,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

observed

Numeric vector of non-negative, whole-number aggregate observed event counts by stratum.

expected

Numeric vector of non-negative expected events by stratum.

measure

Either "SMR" or "SIR".

scale

Positive multiplier for the reported ratio. The conventional value 100 reports percent of expected events; use 1 for an unscaled ratio.

level

Confidence level.

Value

An object of class ds.vertIndirectStandardization containing the observed-to-expected ratio, its scaled estimate, an exact Poisson confidence interval, provenance, and assumptions.

Details

This function is entirely client-side. It makes no DSI or DataSHIELD calls and exposes no new server-side values.

References

Garwood, F. (1936). Fiducial limits for the Poisson distribution. Biometrika, 28, 437–442.
